transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I’m here because I can’t really stop thinking about my face. Like, the left side looks crooked to me, kind of messed up, and I know that sounds weird when I say it out loud.

It’s mostly at work, like at the warehouse when I’m stocking stuff, or even when I go to salsa night — which I used to like, actually, there’s this one song they always play and everyone knows the steps except me half the time — but anyway, I feel like people are noticing my face. They’ll say they don’t see anything, but I still feel like they’re looking at it. Like they can tell something is off.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to make your face look or feel better?

Yeah… I do. Like before I go back out on the inventory floor, I’ll stop in the bathroom and check my face in the mirror. Not just once, it’s like I keep looking, then I fix my cap, rub at that same spot on my face like maybe it’ll sit different or something.

And then I’ll tell myself, okay, go back, but I end up checking again. The bathroom at work has this bad lighting too, it makes everything look worse, and there’s always someone banging on the door or whatever. Sometimes I’m in there so long I’m late getting back, and then my picking numbers fall behind and my boss gets on me again.
Is it just your face that you're worried about, or are there other parts of your body that you think are flawed?

Mostly it’s my face. Like the left side… I can’t stop seeing it as crooked or messed up somehow.

I mean, sometimes I’ll be at the warehouse and someone just glances over while we’re stocking, and I’m already thinking, okay, they noticed it. Same thing at salsa night — which is dumb because people are usually watching feet and trying not to bump into each other — but I still feel like they’re looking at my face. Even when they tell me they don’t see anything, I don’t really believe it.
Are you worried about other things being imperfect or flawed, beyond just your face?

Not really other stuff, no… I mean, I guess everybody has things they don’t like, like my work shoes are always beat up because the warehouse floors are rough, and one time at salsa I wore the wrong shirt and felt stupid, but that’s not the thing.

It’s my face. The left side, specifically. I can’t stop thinking it looks crooked or messed up, and then I’m at work or at salsa night thinking people are noticing it. Even when they say they don’t see anything, I don’t really buy it.
Do these thoughts about your face feel like they're coming into your mind against your will?

Yeah… I mean, it doesn’t feel like I’m choosing to sit there thinking about it. It just kind of jumps in my head, like, I’ll be at the warehouse trying to count boxes or move stuff, and suddenly I’m thinking the left side of my face looks crooked, like somebody noticed it.

Same at salsa night — I’ll be trying to remember the steps, and then I’m wondering if my face looks messed up under the lights. People say they don’t see anything, but it’s hard to believe them. It just keeps coming back even when I’m trying to focus on something else.
Do you try to ignore or push away these thoughts about your face being crooked?

Yeah, I try to, but it doesn’t really work. I’ll tell myself, like, stop thinking about your face, just do your job, count the boxes, whatever… and then I’m right back on it.

It’s mostly that left side. I keep thinking it looks crooked or messed up, and then if someone at the warehouse looks over, I’m like, there it is, they noticed. Same thing at salsa night, even though I know people are supposed to be paying attention to the steps and the music and all that. I try to push it out, but it just keeps coming back, like everyone can see it even when they say they don’t.
Are these thoughts about your face affecting your relationships with friends or family?

Yeah… I mean, it has. I don’t see people as much now. Like, I used to go play soccer and do salsa nights, and my family does these get-togethers where somebody always wants pictures, and I just… I’ve been skipping a lot of that.

It’s not even that I don’t like them. I do. My cousin makes this grilled chicken thing at family stuff, and everybody stands around in the kitchen, and normally I’d be there joking around, but then somebody pulls out a phone and I’m thinking about my face the whole time. So I just don’t go.

And at work, it’s gotten bad too. I’ve been written up at the warehouse because I get delayed, like I’m supposed to be stocking or filling orders and I get caught up worrying people are looking at me. Then I fall behind. So yeah, it’s affecting things.
Do you feel like you're having these thoughts about your face because you want to think about them, or do they just pop into your head?

No, I don’t want to think about it. It just pops in, like I’ll be doing my work at the warehouse and suddenly I’m thinking the left side of my face looks crooked or messed up, and then I’m sure somebody noticed.

It happens at salsa night too, which is annoying because I’m supposed to be thinking about the steps — and the instructor gets all into the music, like counting out loud — but then my mind goes right back to my face. Even when people say they don’t see anything, I still can’t stop thinking everyone can.
Do you feel like these thoughts about your face are unwanted, like they're intruding into your mind?

Yeah, unwanted, definitely. I’m not sitting there trying to think about it. I’m here because I can’t stop thinking the left side of my face looks crooked, like it’s messed up somehow.

Like I’ll be at the warehouse, and I’m supposed to be focused on the orders, and then it just cuts in. Or at salsa night, same thing — everyone’s moving around and I should be paying attention, but I start thinking, they’re noticing it. Even when people say they don’t see anything, I still feel like they do.
Do these thoughts about your face being crooked make you feel anxious or upset?

I mean… I don’t know, anxious is maybe the word? It’s hard to separate it. Like, I’ll notice it and then I’m just not really present anymore.

It’s kind of like when you’re trying to remember if you left the stove on, except I don’t cook that much—my mom always says I eat too much takeout, which is true, there’s this place near my apartment that knows my order now. But yeah, with my face, it just gets in my head and I can’t settle down.
Are these thoughts about your face making it hard for you to do your job or enjoy things you used to like?

Yeah… it is. At work, the warehouse, I’ve actually been written up because I fall behind. Like I’ll be stocking or filling orders and then I get stuck thinking somebody’s looking at my face, and then everything takes longer.

And stuff I used to like… I’ve been skipping soccer, salsa nights, even family things. My cousin is always taking pictures at gatherings — she posts everything, like even the food, which honestly sometimes looks terrible in photos — but I just don’t want to be there if people are looking at me or taking pictures. So I end up not going.
Do you think these thoughts about your face being crooked are reasonable or do they seem irrational to you?

I don’t know. I go back and forth on that. Like, part of me hears people say they don’t see it and I think, okay, maybe I’m making it bigger than it is… but then I look in a mirror or catch myself in a window and it’s like, no, it’s right there.

It’s hard to call it irrational when it feels so obvious to me. But then again, I guess if nobody else is reacting the way I think they are… I don’t know. My brother says I overthink everything, but he says that about stupid stuff too, like how I park too far from the entrance at the grocery store. So I don’t really know what to do with that.
Do you feel like these thoughts about your face are a part of you or do they feel like they are coming from outside of yourself?

I’m not totally sure what you mean by “outside of myself.” Like, it doesn’t feel like a voice or something, if that’s what you mean. It’s more like… it’s my own thought, but it gets so loud in my head that it doesn’t feel like I can just turn it off.

Kind of like when a song gets stuck in your head, except it’s not a song, and it’s not harmless. Actually, there’s this one song they play at work sometimes that drives me crazy, but anyway—yeah, I guess it feels like it’s coming from me, but I don’t feel in control of it.
Do you feel like these thoughts about your face being crooked are in line with how you see yourself as a person?

I’m not sure… like, “in line with how I see myself” is kind of hard to answer.

I don’t think I walk around thinking, like, “I’m a crooked-face guy,” if that’s what you mean. But then when I’m around people, it kind of becomes the main thing I think about. Like at work, if someone looks at me too long, I start thinking that’s what they’re noticing.

I don’t know if that answers it. I guess it feels tied to me somehow, but I don’t really know how to separate it. Also, “how I see myself” changes depending on the day, you know? Like some days I feel normal until I catch a reflection, and then the whole thing is ruined.
Do you feel like thinking about your face being crooked is causing you a lot of emotional pain or distress?

Yeah… I mean, that’s pretty much why I’m here. It’s not like I just notice it once and move on. I keep thinking the left side of my face looks crooked, like messed up, and then I can’t stop checking whether people notice it.

At the warehouse, if somebody looks at me while we’re talking or even just walking past, I start thinking, okay, they see it. And at salsa night too, which is stupid because you’re supposed to be focused on the music and steps—like the instructor keeps saying to keep your frame up, and I’m thinking about my face instead.

So yeah, it causes a lot of distress. Even when people tell me they don’t see anything, I don’t really believe it, or I believe it for like five minutes and then it comes back.
Do you think people would judge you or treat you differently if they actually saw the flaw in your face that you're worried about?

Yeah, I do. That’s kind of the part I can’t get away from. Like if they really saw it the way I see it—the left side of my face looking crooked and messed up—I feel like they’d think something was wrong with me, or they’d look at me differently.

At the warehouse, even if somebody’s just asking where a pallet goes, I’m thinking, “They’re noticing it.” And at salsa night too, which is embarrassing because I’m supposed to be counting steps and not staring at people’s reactions. People tell me they don’t see anything, but I don’t know… it doesn’t stick. I’m here because I can’t stop thinking about it.
Have you avoided any important work or social activities because of your concerns about your face?

Yeah… I have. More than I want to admit, I guess.

Work has gotten affected too, not just social stuff. I’ve been written up at the warehouse because I get delayed, like I’ll get stuck worrying about people seeing my face or I’ll try to avoid certain areas if there are too many people around. And then the order doesn’t get done fast enough.

Social stuff is worse, honestly. I used to go play soccer, and I’ve been skipping that. Salsa nights too, even though I actually like it when I can just focus on it. And family gatherings… I’ve missed some because somebody always wants pictures, or there’s a group photo, and then I’m thinking about where to stand and which side of my face is showing. It just feels easier not to go.
Is it always the left side of your face that you think looks crooked, or are there other features that sometimes catch your attention as well?

It’s mostly the left side, yeah. That’s the thing I keep getting stuck on — like it looks crooked or messed up somehow.

I mean, sometimes I’ll start noticing other little things if I’m already in that headspace, but it always comes back to the left side of my face. Like at the warehouse, someone will glance at me and I’m thinking, “They see it.” Or at salsa night, I’m supposed to be paying attention to the steps, and instead I’m wondering if my face looks off from that angle.

Even when people say they don’t notice anything, I don’t know… I can’t really hold onto that. It just comes right back.
When you think about your face being crooked, are you more concerned about it not being symmetrical or about what other people might think of you?

I guess it starts with the symmetry thing, like the left side just looks crooked or messed up to me. But it turns into what people think pretty fast.

Like at the warehouse, I’ll be trying to do my job and then I’m thinking, are they noticing it? Same thing at salsa night… I’m supposed to be following the music, but I’m watching people’s faces to see if they see what I see. And even when someone says they don’t notice anything, I don’t really believe it for long.

So… both, I guess. But the part I can’t stop thinking about is that everyone can see it and is judging me for it.

Yeah, I do. That’s kind of the part I can’t get away from. Like if they really saw it the way I see it—the left side of my face looking crooked and messed up—I feel like they’d think something was wrong with me, or they’d look at me differently.

At the warehouse, even if somebody’s just asking where a pallet goes, I’m thinking, “They’re noticing it.” And at salsa night too, which is embarrassing because I’m supposed to be counting steps and not staring at people’s reactions. People tell me they don’t see anything, but I don’t know… it doesn’t stick. I’m here because I can’t stop thinking about it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thoughts about their face being crooked are causing significant impairment in social or occupational functioning
doctor.question: Have you avoided any important work or social activities because of your concerns about your face?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment

patient.answer:
Yeah… I have. More than I want to admit, I guess.

Work has gotten affected too, not just social stuff. I’ve been written up at the warehouse because I get delayed, like I’ll get stuck worrying about people seeing my face or I’ll try to avoid certain areas if there are too many people around. And then the order doesn’t get done fast enough.

Social stuff is worse, honestly. I used to go play soccer, and I’ve been skipping that. Salsa nights too, even though I actually like it when I can just focus on it. And family gatherings… I’ve missed some because somebody always wants pictures, or there’s a group photo, and then I’m thinking about where to stand and which side of my face is showing. It just feels easier not to go.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's concerns are focused on a specific perceived flaw
doctor.question: Is it always the left side of your face that you think looks crooked, or are there other features that sometimes catch your attention as well?

target_item.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because I can’t stop thinking that the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up, like everyone at the warehouse or at salsa night is noticing it even when they tell me they don’t see anything.

patient.answer:
It’s mostly the left side, yeah. That’s the thing I keep getting stuck on — like it looks crooked or messed up somehow.

I mean, sometimes I’ll start noticing other little things if I’m already in that headspace, but it always comes back to the left side of my face. Like at the warehouse, someone will glance at me and I’m thinking, “They see it.” Or at salsa night, I’m supposed to be paying attention to the steps, and instead I’m wondering if my face looks off from that angle.

Even when people say they don’t notice anything, I don’t know… I can’t really hold onto that. It just comes right back.

patient.answer:
I guess it starts with the symmetry thing, like the left side just looks crooked or messed up to me. But it turns into what people think pretty fast.

Like at the warehouse, I’ll be trying to do my job and then I’m thinking, are they noticing it? Same thing at salsa night… I’m supposed to be following the music, but I’m watching people’s faces to see if they see what I see. And even when someone says they don’t notice anything, I don’t really believe it for long.

So… both, I guess. But the part I can’t stop thinking about is that everyone can see it and is judging me for it.
